name: Every photo move has a reason
when: Any still photo that gets a Ken Burns move
action: Move toward what the narration is talking about. Push in = focus on a detail. Pull out = reveal where we are. Pan = follow a direction (a road, a gaze, steps going up). If you cannot say in one line why the frame moves, hold it still.
why: Ken Burns and his editors: movement without meaning is noise; motion also decides what the viewer looks at, so it can change the meaning of the photo.
evidence_note: Ken Burns and documentary editors quoted in Poynter (craft article) + 43frames craft blog agree. No numbers here, so it is a judgement rule.
conflict_note: Extends R-205 (har beat action) and R-220 (zoom in = zor). Does not replace them.

name: Ken Burns size: 10–20% scale change
when: Ken Burns move on a still
action: Change scale by about 10–20% over the whole clip (e.g. 100%→112%). Below ~8% the move is invisible; above ~30% people watch the camera, not the photo. Keep one direction per still.
why: Big zooms feel like an effect and expose low resolution.
evidence_note: One craft blog gives the numbers (43frames); no official source publishes them. Treat as a starting value.
conflict_note: Different job from R-329 (push-in 2–6% in 1–1.5 s, for UI/product camera moves) and R-428 (105–110% emphasis zoom). G-002 is for a full-length slow move on a narration still. R-296 (100↔112% punch) is a cut, not a move.

name: Never zoom past the photo's pixels
when: Choosing Ken Burns end frame for any still
action: Max zoom = source pixels ÷ output pixels (check width AND height). Example: 3000 px wide photo on a 1920 px timeline allows 1.56×. If the photo is smaller than the frame, do not zoom: use a static hold, a smaller move, or a different photo. Set the crop on the original resolution, not on a pre-scaled copy.
why: Past that ratio every frame is upscaled and goes soft exactly where the viewer is looking.
evidence_note: Plain arithmetic, shown the same way in 43frames and in the PTE AV Studio manual (manual is CC BY-NC-SA: idea only, not copied).
conflict_note: No existing rule covers resolution headroom. Note: a 4K master needs ~2× more source pixels than 1080p for the same move.

name: How long a still can stay on screen
when: Narration-led still photo in long-form
action: Give a moving still about 4–8 s. Under ~3 s the move reads as a twitch; past ~8–10 s a single photo drifts. If a still must stay longer, slow the move or split it into two framings of the same photo (wide, then detail).
why: The move needs time to register, but one photo cannot hold attention forever.
evidence_note: From one craft blog (43frames: 6–8 s, <4 hurried, >10 drifts). No official number exists.
conflict_note: Conflicts with R-432 (B-roll hold 1.2–3.0 s) and R-136 (verticals 2–3 s). Proposed split: long-form narration stills 4–8 s; Reels/montage stills 2–3 s with a smaller or no move. R-134/R-158 visual-change cadence can be met by a second framing of the same photo.

name: Ease every move, one axis at a time
when: Any Ken Burns or map camera move
action: Always ease in and ease out; never linear. Use one axis per still (push OR pan), not a random diagonal drift.
why: Linear start/stop looks robotic and is the most common amateur tell.
evidence_note: 43frames quotes Apple Final Cut docs on automatic ease; PTE manual says linear gives jerky motion. Two sources agree.
conflict_note: Duplicates R-261 (easing never linear) and R-328 (no zoom+pan together). Keep as the still-photo version; can be merged.

name: Vary moves across a photo run
when: Two or more stills in a row
action: Alternate push-in, pull-out and pan; change the start edge; leave some stills completely still. No more than 2 identical moves (same type + same direction) in a row. A shot that ends pushing in cuts well into one that starts wide.
why: Twenty photos drifting the same way turn a story into wallpaper; a still frame after moving ones reads as emphasis.
evidence_note: One craft blog (43frames). Max-2 number is our proposal.
conflict_note: Overlaps R-244 (alternate zooms in neighbouring segments) and R-426 (decorative runs <4). G-006 is the still-specific, stricter version.

name: New place: wide first, then detail
when: First time a new place (temple, ghat, town) appears
action: Open the place with a wide/establishing image (or the map, G-026) before details. Inside a place you may also start tight on one detail and pull out to reveal it — but do that on purpose, once, not as the default.
why: Viewer must know where they are before details mean anything; a deliberate reveal is a storytelling device.
evidence_note: Documentary editors in Poynter describe both patterns (start wide and move in / start tight and reveal). Matches R-397.
conflict_note: Duplicates R-397 (establish → detail → reaction → widen) and R-432 (wide → medium → close). Adds only the "first mention of a place" trigger.

name: Parallax (2.5D) is a spice, not the base
when: Any 2.5D/parallax still
action: Use parallax only on hero stills (opening, chapter openers, payoff), keep layer offsets small, never two parallax shots back to back, never on deity images (G-021). Prefer flat Ken Burns for the rest.
why: W3C names parallax as a known trigger of dizziness and nausea for people with vestibular disorders; fake depth on cut-out edges also looks cheap.
evidence_note: W3C WCAG 2.3.3 Understanding doc confirms the health risk (official, permissive licence). The usage limits are our proposal — no source gives numbers.
conflict_note: Adds limits on top of R-356 (depth ratios 0.2/0.5/1.0), which says how, not how often.

name: Graphics inside the 16:9 safe area
when: Every text, card, label, logo in the 16:9 master
action: Keep all graphics inside a 5% inset from every edge (graphics/title safe). Keep essential action inside a 3.5% inset. At 1920×1080: graphics x 96–1824, y 54–1026.
why: Broadcast standard so text is never cut by overscan, rounded TV corners or player chrome.
evidence_note: EBU R 95 v1.1 (official broadcast recommendation).
conflict_note: New: existing R-095 only covers 9:16. Also: keep text clear of YouTube end-screen element area in last 5–20 s (R-016).

name: 9:16 safe zone — use the official numbers
when: Every text/graphic in the Reels/Shorts 9:16 export
action: Keep text, pop words, captions, logos inside: top 14% clear, bottom 35% clear, 6% each side, and right 10% clear for the YouTube Shorts button rail. Combined box: x 6–90%, y 14–65% (1080×1920: x 65–972, y 269–1248).
why: Meta (Reels) and Google (Shorts) both say UI covers these bands; captions placed lower get hidden under the caption/CTA/like buttons.
evidence_note: Meta Ads Guide Reels spec (14/35/6) and Google Shorts ads page (top 10, bottom 25, right 10). Both are ad guidance; applied to organic posts as the safe, conservative choice.
conflict_note: CORRECTS R-095 (y_max 79 / captions at y≈78% would sit inside Meta's 35% bottom band) and R-254/R-124 pixel insets. If Meta disclaimer text is used, bottom 40% clear. Organic UI is smaller, so this is stricter than needed — on purpose.

name: No flashing faster than 3 per second
when: Flash transitions, strobe pop words, lightning/aarti-flame flicker, fast white flashes
action: Nothing may flash more than 3 times in any 1 second (large bright or red flashes). Flash transitions: max 1 per cut, never in a chain.
why: Flashing above this can trigger seizures; it is the web/TV safety threshold.
evidence_note: W3C WCAG 2.3.1 (official). Checkable from effect timings.
conflict_note: New. R-424 (hard-reject transitions) can list flash chains.

name: Number cards: count, then hold
when: Animated numbers (₹ price, km, steps, timings)
action: Count-up ≤ ~1.2 s, then hold the final number at least max(1.5 s, words × 0.3 s). The final value lands on the spoken number (±0.5 s). Keep units with the number (₹, km, min).
why: People read the final value, not the rolling digits; BBC minimum reading time is ~0.3 s per word.
evidence_note: BBC subtitle guideline gives 0.3 s/word at 160–180 wpm (official). Count duration is from R-303.
conflict_note: Builds on R-303 (0.3 s delay, 1.2 s count) and R-091 (reading formula). No conflict.

name: Hindi/Hinglish caption speed
when: Every Hinglish (Roman) caption cue
action: Target ≤ 20 characters per second; hard ceiling 22 cps. Max 42 characters per line, max 2 lines, prefer 1 line. If over, split the cue or shorten words — do not paraphrase meaning.
why: Netflix sets Hindi adult subtitles at up to 22 cps and 42 chars/line; Roman Hinglish is longer in characters than Devanagari, so a lower target is safer.
evidence_note: Netflix Hindi Timed Text Style Guide (22 cps, 42 chars, 2 lines). The 20 cps target is our safety margin.
conflict_note: CONFLICT: R-131 says ≤17 cps (that is a European-language number, e.g. Netflix Brazilian Portuguese = 17). R-092 says ≤20. For Hindi/Hinglish use 20 target / 22 max. Burned-in word-chunk styles (R-247, R-259) are exempt from cps but not from G-014 durations.

name: Caption timing: Netflix rules
when: Every caption cue
action: Min 20 frames (5/6 s), max 7 s. Gap between cues is either exactly 2 frames or ≥ 0.5 s — never 3–11 frames (at 24 fps; scale for 25/30). If speech ends and no cue follows, hold 0.5 s more. If an in/out time is within 0.5 s of a cut, snap it to the cut (out = 2 frames before cut). Do not cross a cut unless the speech does.
why: Even gaps and cut-aligned captions stop the "flashy" blink and make reading effortless.
evidence_note: Netflix General Requirements + Subtitle Timing Guidelines (official).
conflict_note: Duplicates R-092 (20 frames, 2-frame gap) and R-131 (1–7 s). Adds the 3–11 frame ban, cut snapping and 0.5 s linger. R-093 (cue does not cross join) agrees.

name: Line breaks that respect Hindi grammar
when: Splitting a Hinglish caption into 2 lines or 2 cues
action: Break after punctuation or before a conjunction (aur, lekin, par, ki, to). Never split a noun from its postposition (“Dwarka | me”, “mandir | ke”), a first name from surname, a verb from its helper (“ja | rahe hain”). Prefer bottom-heavy shape but not 1–2 words alone on top.
why: Wrong breaks force re-reading; Hindi postpositions come after the noun, so the English article rule maps to postpositions.
evidence_note: Netflix general line-break rules + Netflix Hindi line treatment (official); the postposition mapping is our adaptation.
conflict_note: Refines R-092 (English break rules). No conflict.

name: One spelling list (glossary) for every place and name
when: Any place/deity/ritual name in captions, cards, map labels, chapters, titles
action: Keep one Hinglish spelling glossary per video (e.g. Dwarkadhish, Gomti Ghat, Jagat Mandir, darshan, aarti) and use it everywhere. Never translate proper names. Check every text layer against it before export.
why: Netflix requires a key-names list for consistency; mixed spellings (Dwarkadheesh / Dwarkadhish) look careless and break search.
evidence_note: Netflix General Requirements §6 (KNP consistency) and Hindi guide (do not translate proper names) — official.
conflict_note: New. Machine-checkable by string match.

name: Caption vs on-screen text: no clash, no repeat
when: A card, pop word or map label is on screen while captions run
action: If a card/label sits in the caption zone, move the caption to the top (centre) for that cue. If the pop word just repeats the caption word, keep the caption and make the pop word the highlighted caption word instead of a second copy. Never put two different texts in the same place at the same time.
why: Netflix: position subtitles to avoid on-screen text; delete redundant on-screen-text subtitles. Two texts at once split attention (R-318).
evidence_note: Netflix General Requirements §5 (positioning) and Hindi guide §I.8 (redundant FN deleted) — official, adapted.
conflict_note: Softer than R-376 (captions OFF in title zones). Proposal: for narration-led video keep captions on but move them; switch them off only for the hero title (R-436).

name: Text contrast numbers
when: Any text over a photo or video
action: Text vs its background ≥ 4.5:1; large text (≥ 24 px-equivalent bold-ish, i.e. ~18 pt) may go to 3:1. Over busy photos always add a scrim/box or outline — measure contrast against the scrim.
why: Official minimum for people with weaker vision; also needed for phones in sunlight.
evidence_note: W3C WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 (official).
conflict_note: Upgrades R-096 (already says ≥4.5:1) to 🟢 and adds the 3:1 large-text allowance for pop words/titles.

name: No inside-sanctum images unless official
when: Any temple video, esp. Dwarkadhish
action: Do not use photos or clips from inside the Dwarkadhish sanctum/darshan area unless they come from the temple or a source with clear permission. Use exterior, shikhara, Gomti Ghat, courtyard, crowd-from-outside images. Never present an unknown "inside" image as ours.
why: Phones and photography are not allowed in the sanctum; security checks are enforced and phones can be confiscated. Using such footage invites complaints and takedowns, and it disrespects the rule devotees follow.
evidence_note: Independent local guide (devbhumidwarka.in, opened). Other search results said the same and mentioned a district notification and a police case, but those pages were NOT opened — verify with the temple trust before publishing.
conflict_note: Extends R-019 (licensed media only). Human must confirm per temple.

name: Calm treatment for deity (murti) images
when: Any frame where a deity / murti / sacred symbol is the subject
action: Only static hold or a slow push-in (≤ G-002 range). No zoom-punch, shake, glitch, whip, spin, mirror, warp, speed-ramp, flash, emoji, comic SFX or meme pop words on these frames. Cut or soft dissolve only.
why: Images that may offend religious groups need special care (BBC); devotees see the murti as sacred, and flashy effects read as mockery.
evidence_note: BBC Editorial Guidelines stills guidance + HAF guidance give the principle (care, no degrading modification). The specific effect list is our inference — get a devotee/human check.
conflict_note: Overrides R-200/R-296/R-145 (punch-ins), R-428 (emphasis zoom) and R-422 (motion accents) on deity-tagged beats. In ORDER.md this should sit at Kahani level (offence = story failure).

name: Never cover or alter the murti
when: Text/graphics near a deity image
action: No caption, pop word, sticker, logo or arrow over the deity's face or body; place text in empty areas or use a different crop. Do not recolour, cut out, parallax-separate or composite the deity.
why: HAF lists "significant material modification of a Deity" as likely to offend; covering the face is the visual version of that.
evidence_note: HAF guidance (principle) — the screen-layout rule is our adaptation.
conflict_note: Like R-246 (cards never on a face) but for the murti. Blocks G-008 parallax on deity images.

name: Pilgrims are people, not props
when: Identifiable worshippers, priests, bathers at ghats
action: Do not zoom in on identifiable people praying or bathing unless they agreed. Prefer wide or from-behind shots; blur faces of people who did not agree. No pop words or jokes over people at prayer.
why: An image in a public place can still be private (BBC); many pilgrims are there for private vows.
evidence_note: BBC stills guidance (privacy in public places) + local guide (ask first, blur unwilling faces).
conflict_note: New.

name: Devotional words: accurate and calm
when: Titles, cards and pop words in temple/darshan sections
action: Use correct names (Dwarkadhish, Jagat Mandir) from the glossary (G-016). Avoid hype or slang pop words ("CRAZY", "OMG") on rituals; prefer factual or devotional words (darshan, aarti, dhwaja). Captions must state facts correctly.
why: BBC: captions that accompany images must be factually correct and images must not reinforce stereotypes; wrong names offend devotees.
evidence_note: Principle from BBC stills guidance; word choices are our inference.
conflict_note: Narrows R-121 (power words) for devotional beats.

name: Map only when it helps
when: A new destination, a leg of travel, or a distance/time number is spoken
action: Show a map at the first mention of a new place or leg, or when a distance/travel time is said. Not for every place name. One map beat per chapter plus an optional route recap at the end.
why: A map tells the viewer where they are and what comes next; too many maps become filler.
evidence_note: Craft/vendor guides (ClickPop, Animaps). No official source.
conflict_note: Applies R-089 (graphic only when it explains) and R-364 (route must be clear) to maps.

name: Route draw timing
when: Animated route line
action: Optional whole-route overview 1.5–2 s. Each leg draws in 1.5–3 s (longer legs a bit longer; never > 8 s). On arrival: ~0.5 s still, then the label. The line should finish as the narration names the destination. End recap 2–3 s.
why: Fast enough to feel like travel, slow enough to follow; finishing on the spoken name locks picture to words.
evidence_note: ClickPop guide gives the leg/arrival/ending numbers; Animaps agrees on holds. Vendor guides — starting values.
conflict_note: Fits R-199 (animation payoff lands on the spoken word).

name: Map holds for reading
when: After any map camera move or label reveal
action: Hold ≥ 2 s after each camera move, ~1 s extra per short label (1–3 words), 2–3 s for a 6–10 word line, 3–4 s on the final full view. On Reels cut stops, not pauses.
why: If the map moves on before people finish reading, the label is wasted.
evidence_note: Animaps guide (vendor). Consistent with BBC 0.3 s/word.
conflict_note: Map-specific version of R-091.

name: Phone-readable map design
when: Designing any map frame
action: Max 4 labels visible; current stop biggest. Route line ~10–16 px on a 1080-wide canvas, one bright colour with a dark outline. Muted 2–3 tone base map. One camera move per leg (no constant spin). Labels flat and facing the viewer. In 9:16 keep the route inside the middle 60% and the G-010 box.
why: Maps are dense; phones need fewer, bigger things.
evidence_note: ClickPop guide (vendor).
conflict_note: Consistent with R-252 (2 accents) and R-318 (max two demands per frame).

name: Real map data, credited
when: Building any map
action: Build maps from real data you may use (e.g. OpenStreetMap with its attribution) — never let a generator invent roads or coastlines. Put the attribution in the description or end card. For India, show official boundaries; if unsure, flag for human check.
why: Invented geography is a factual error; open data licences require attribution.
evidence_note: ClickPop guide says open data like OSM needs attribution and warns against generated maps. India-boundary point is our caution, not researched here.
conflict_note: Extends R-018 (no invented facts) and R-019 (licensed media).

name: Platform length limits (verified)
when: Cutting a Short/Reel from the long video
action: YouTube Shorts: up to 3:00 if vertical or square (uploads after 15 Oct 2024). Instagram Reels: up to 3 min can be recommended to non-followers (announced Jan 2025, US first). A Short over 1:00 with any active Content ID claim is blocked worldwide — so any Short > 60 s must have fully cleared/own audio.
why: Hard platform facts; the 60 s Content ID rule can silently kill a Short.
evidence_note: YouTube Help 15424877 and Instagram Creators blog (official).
conflict_note: CORRECTS R-172 ("max recommended 60 s" for Reels is outdated as a limit) and widens R-026/R-073 windows as limits (their 20–60 s remain good targets). Audio note is for the later audio phase.

name: Re-frame stills for 9:16, don't centre-crop
when: Making Reels from 16:9 stills/clips
action: Re-set each Ken Burns start/end window on the 9:16 crop so the subject stays inside the G-010 box for the whole move. Never auto centre-crop a 16:9 timeline. If the subject cannot fit, use a different photo.
why: Platforms crop/scale vertical video and UI covers top and bottom; a centred crop often cuts the temple spire or the face.
evidence_note: Google Ads vertical-video help (cropping behaviour) + Meta safe zone (official); the method is our adaptation.
conflict_note: Builds on R-218 (reframe on subject) and R-255 (re-layout first).

name: Short hook: first second
when: First frame of every Reel/Short
action: Frame 1 must already show the strongest image + a short on-screen hook (≤ 7 words, inside G-010). No logo, no greeting, no fade-in from black.
why: Shorts viewers swipe within about a second (creator view published on the official YouTube blog).
evidence_note: YouTube official blog quoting a top Shorts creator — an informed opinion, not data.
conflict_note: Duplicates R-111 (1-second rule), R-001, R-005 (hook ≤7 words), R-044. Only adds the "no fade from black" item.

name: Chapters and end screen (verified)
when: Long-form YouTube upload
action: Chapters: first at 00:00, at least 3, ascending, each ≥ 10 s; use glossary spellings (G-016). End screen: last 5–20 s, video ≥ 25 s, up to 4 elements on 16:9; keep that area free of key text.
why: Official YouTube rules.
evidence_note: YouTube Help 9884579 and 6388789 (official), opened 2026-11-06.
conflict_note: Exact duplicate of R-087 and R-016 — use to upgrade both to 🟢, then drop this rule.

name: Motion duration bands (UI scale)
when: Text card / label / pop-word entrances and exits
action: Small elements 150–300 ms, medium moves 250–400 ms, large/full-screen 450–600 ms, ambient up to 1000 ms. Exits shorter than entrances.
why: Published design-system durations; keeps motion consistent across all cards.
evidence_note: Material Design 3 duration tokens (official Google design system).
conflict_note: Corroborates R-202 (0.35–0.6 s), R-299 (0.4–1.2 s), R-353 (UI 0.3–0.5 s) and R-315 (exit faster). R-299 upper 1.2 s is above Material's 1.0 s extra-long max — suggest capping at 1.0 s.
